en.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights Allah's strategic 'allowance' (tadhir) of the disbeliever, often identified as Abu Jahl, to proceed in his misguidance as a form of gradual punishment and divine wisdom. The term 'khalaqtu wahidan' emphasizes the unique creation of the disbeliever without a father, underscing his solitary accountability before God. This reflects the principle that divine decree permits the path of the misguided to remain open until the appointed time of reckoning.

El término 'jalaktu wahīdan' enfatiza la creación única del incrédulo sin padre, subrayando su responsabilidad solitaria ante Dios. Esto refleja el principio de que el decreto divino permite que el camino del extraviado permanezca abierto hasta el momento designado del juicio.
